target.queryText:
SELECT MIN(t.executed_ts) AS time,
       i.symbol || ' ' || t.side || ' ' || SUM(t.quantity) || ' @ '
         || printf('%.2f', SUM(t.quantity * t.price) / SUM(t.quantity))
         || CASE WHEN n.sentiment IS NULL THEN '' ELSE ' - ' || n.sentiment END
         || CASE WHEN n.note IS NULL THEN '' ELSE ': ' || n.note END AS text,
       t.side || COALESCE(',' || n.sentiment, '') AS tags
FROM trade_note n
JOIN trade t ON t.id = n.trade_id
JOIN instrument i ON i.id = t.instrument_id
WHERE t.side = 'BUY'
GROUP BY i.symbol, t.session_date, t.side, COALESCE(t.order_id, 'at' || t.executed_ts), n.sentiment, n.note
ORDER BY MIN(t.executed_ts)
LIMIT 500

panels.title: Latest readings, and how far they have moved
panels.description:
Each series' newest daily reading and its date, then the move since the reading a month, three months and a year before it.

- **Yields** move in basis points (bp): 25 bp is a quarter of a percentage point. Higher US yields pull foreign money out of emerging markets, India's included, and lift the dollar against the rupee.
- **Prices** move in percent. India imports most of its oil, so dearer crude widens the trade deficit, weakens the rupee and squeezes the margins of oil marketers, paints, tyres and airlines.
- **Gold and silver** rise when money leaves riskier assets, and with the rupee's fall, since MCX prices them in rupees off the dollar price. A rally in them alongside falling shares is money looking for safety.

The yields are the US Treasury's daily par yield curve rates, from the Treasury the evening after the US trading day. Brent and WTI are the EIA's daily spot prices, from the open oil-prices dataset (github.com/datasets/oil-prices), which refreshes them weekly, so they run about a week behind. MCX crude oil, gold and silver are the day's closing price of whichever of their futures traded most that day, from Groww, read the evening after. Gold and silver are per troy ounce (31.1 g): MCX quotes gold per 10 grams and silver per kilogram, so the price on Groww's page is this one divided by 3.11 for gold, and multiplied by 32.15 for silver. The buttons above have today's prices.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH names(series, name, kind, position, per) AS (
  VALUES ('US10Y', 'US 10-year Treasury yield', 'yield', 1, 1),
         ('US2Y', 'US 2-year Treasury yield', 'yield', 2, 1),
         ('BRENT', 'Brent crude (USD a barrel)', 'usd', 3, 1),
         ('WTI', 'WTI crude (USD a barrel)', 'usd', 4, 1),
         ('MCX_CRUDEOIL', 'MCX crude oil (₹ a barrel)', 'inr', 5, 1),
         ('MCX_GOLD', 'MCX gold (₹ a troy ounce)', 'inr', 6, 3.11034768),
         ('MCX_SILVER', 'MCX silver (₹ a troy ounce)', 'inr', 7, 0.0311034768)),
latest AS (
  SELECT n.name, n.kind, n.position, n.per, m.series, m.observed_on, m.value
  FROM names n
  JOIN market_series m ON m.series = n.series
  WHERE m.observed_on = (SELECT MAX(x.observed_on) FROM market_series x WHERE x.series = n.series)),
back AS (
  SELECT l.*,
         (SELECT b.value FROM market_series b WHERE b.series = l.series AND b.observed_on <= date(l.observed_on, '-1 month')
           ORDER BY b.observed_on DESC LIMIT 1) AS month_ago,
         (SELECT b.value FROM market_series b WHERE b.series = l.series AND b.observed_on <= date(l.observed_on, '-3 months')
           ORDER BY b.observed_on DESC LIMIT 1) AS quarter_ago,
         (SELECT b.value FROM market_series b WHERE b.series = l.series AND b.observed_on <= date(l.observed_on, '-1 year')
           ORDER BY b.observed_on DESC LIMIT 1) AS year_ago
  FROM latest l)
SELECT name AS "Series",
       CASE kind WHEN 'yield' THEN printf('%.2f%%', value)
                 WHEN 'usd' THEN printf('%.2f', value)
                 ELSE printf('%,d', CAST(ROUND(value * per) AS INTEGER)) END AS "Latest",
       CAST(strftime('%d', observed_on) AS INTEGER) || ' '
         || substr('JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec', (CAST(strftime('%m', observed_on) AS INTEGER) - 1) * 3 + 1, 3)
         || ' ' || strftime('%Y', observed_on) AS "As of",
       CASE WHEN month_ago IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN kind = 'yield' THEN printf('%+d bp', CAST(ROUND((value - month_ago) * 100) AS INTEGER))
            ELSE printf('%+.1f%%', (value / month_ago - 1) * 100) END AS "Over a month",
       CASE WHEN quarter_ago IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN kind = 'yield' THEN printf('%+d bp', CAST(ROUND((value - quarter_ago) * 100) AS INTEGER))
            ELSE printf('%+.1f%%', (value / quarter_ago - 1) * 100) END AS "Over 3 months",
       CASE WHEN year_ago IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN kind = 'yield' THEN printf('%+d bp', CAST(ROUND((value - year_ago) * 100) AS INTEGER))
            ELSE printf('%+.1f%%', (value / year_ago - 1) * 100) END AS "Over a year"
FROM back
ORDER BY position

panels.title: US Treasury yields (%)
panels.description: The 10- and 2-year yields, and the gap between them (right axis). A gap below zero, an inverted curve, has come before most US recessions; the gap widening back out of one has often come as a slowdown arrives.

panels.title: MCX crude oil (₹ a barrel)
panels.description: MCX's crude oil future, which follows WTI in rupees: the day's close of whichever contract traded most. Against WTI above, it adds the rupee's own move against the dollar. Groww has candles only for contracts still trading, so the line starts when the oldest of them was listed, a few months back, and grows each evening.
